hook_text: The thirty seconds that save nine rand
clip_script:
Here is why we estimate. You buy three things: twelve rand seventy-five, eight rand thirty, and twenty-three rand ninety-five. Before the cashier scans anything, round in your head: about thirteen, about eight, about twenty-four. Thirteen and eight is twenty-one, and twenty-four more is forty-five. So the total should be about forty-five rand. Now the slip prints fifty-four rand. Something is wrong — and because you estimated, you know it before you tap your card.

Let us do the exact sum the careful way, commas lined up. Twelve comma seven five, eight comma three zero, twenty-three comma nine five. Hundredths: five plus zero plus five is ten, write zero, carry one. Tenths: seven plus three plus nine plus the carry is twenty, write zero, carry two. Units: two plus eight plus three plus two is fifteen, write five, carry one. Tens: one plus two plus the carry is four. Forty-five comma zero zero.
visual_style: A till slip printing, a fuel gauge and a medicine syringe, each with a rough estimate flashing beside the exact figure
call_to_action: Open the full session to make estimating a reflex.
